chapter: After the road: New York, the profession and advice
title: Mr. Collins's Harlem restaurant and rooming house
summary: Musicians like Don Byas and Hinton roomed at Mr. Collins's place for a few dollars a week and owed him when he died.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But I can the honesty of that. That goes back to like the people did the same thing for Mr. Collins back from Harlem on Seventh Avenue and 127th Street.
Oh, another good place to eat that we didn't mention.
But musicians owed Mr. Collins when he died, though, because a lot of them had rooms. You know, Don Byas used to room up there.
Right. I used to room there. I had a room there one time.
We had no place else to go.
$6 a week and 50 cents for my food.
At the Woodside I was paying eight and a quarter a week.
